anatomy.title: Anatomy of a Prosecution
anatomy.subtitle: One transaction — lawful in arbitration, criminal in the indictment.
anatomy.text: We are not asking for an acquittal. We are asking that every piece of evidence on the record be weighed — including binding arbitration rulings and the investigators' own protocols. This site maps the case layer by layer, from a commercial contract to extradition and international remedies. The files speak for themselves.
anatomy.manifesto: Treat this request as lawful and you normalise a Pandora's box: extradition as cross-border score-settling, where paperwork outweighs a person's life and the requesting state's own final court rulings.

legal.title: Legal dissonance
legal.text: Russian arbitration, through to the Supreme Court, upheld the transaction. The criminal case calls the same facts fraud. Investigators quoted 'value must be real' — then cited it as proof of a conspiracy to understate.
legal.question: How can insisting on fair market value prove a plot to hide it?

international.title: International track
international.text: Serbia, Interpol, the CCF, UNHCR, the ECHR — bodies built to test whether the rule of law holds when domestic systems fail.

actors.title: Who's in the file
actors.text: Who opened the case, who signed the papers, who ruled at each stage — names and dates, not commentary.

flagrant.title: Flagrant Denial of Justice
flagrant.text: Not a single Russian authority — courts, prosecutors, or General Prosecutor — reviewed the complaints on the merits. 8+ identical responses from the Moscow Region Prosecutor, 5 petitions to the General Prosecutor, refusal by Moscow City Court — zero substantive findings. Under ECHR standards this is an independent ground to refuse extradition.
